title: Functorial span square-completion rule
statement: For a category $\mathcal C$ [def-nagata-category] and a wide subcategory $U$, a functorial span square-completion rule assigns to every span $D\xleftarrow{q}B\xrightarrow{h}B\prime$ with $q\in U$ an object $D\prime$ and arrows $D\xrightarrow{k}D\prime\xleftarrow{q\prime}B\prime$ with $q\prime\in U$ and $kq=q\prime h$, and assigns to every commuting triple of maps of input spans a map of output vertices commuting with $k$ and $q\prime$, preserving identities and composition.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, Proposition 8.2(i), printed p. 29 (PDF p. 13), square-completion data used in the following Proofs paragraph.
